indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: One credit card or bank account is used to book travel to or accommodation and transportation in an area of known ISIS activity for several unrelated people at the same time for no known legitimate purpose.
indicators.red_flag: Single instrument funds travel/lodging for multiple unrelated people into a known-ISIS area
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: Fundraisers are attached to social media profiles that show support for ISIS or display ISIS-related iconography or refer to supporting the “mujahideen” or the “war against kufar (non-believers),” especially if the fundraisers are soliciting donations to fund travel to an area of known ISIS activity.
indicators.red_flag: Donation inflows tied to ISIS-supportive social-media fundraisers (adverse-media linkage)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer collects small amounts through P2P transfers, social media, or virtual currency payments over a short period of time and then sends them in a lump sum to an individual located in a region where ISIS presence is prevalent.
indicators.red_flag: Small-amount P2P/VC funnel-in then lump-sum forward to ISIS-prevalent region (collector-aggregator)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C3 (Multi-originator funnel-in / fan-out network detection).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer sends remittances with no known legitimate purpose from the United States to multiple individuals in jurisdictions, such as Türkiye, known for ISIS facilitation activity who do not appear to have any relation to the sender.
indicators.red_flag: Fan-out remittances to no-relationship payees in ISIS-facilitation corridors
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer attempts to purchase plane or other travel tickets after abruptly liquidating assets, closing accounts, cancelling subscriptions, or receiving large unexplained sums of cash.  A period of account dormancy following these behaviors should also be regarded as suspicious, even if the customer eventually resumes transactions within the United States.
indicators.red_flag: Abrupt asset liquidation → travel purchase → account dormancy (pre-travel divestment)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer abruptly appears to seek as many lines of credit as possible, for example, by acquiring several credit cards and taking out one or more loans for unclear reasons, especially if the customer has not used credit cards or taken out loans in the past.  This behavior should be regarded as especially suspicious if the customer uses newly obtained credit cards either exclusively or almost exclusively for cash advances and purchases of virtual currencies but then fails to make loan or credit card payments when they come due.
indicators.red_flag: Sudden credit-line maximization → cash-advance / VC spend → default (bust-out)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer begins receiving a sudden influx of unexplained cash deposits, especially if that customer is unemployed or these deposits are in addition to a regular paycheck, or if the deposits come from ATMs in locations where ISIS is prevalent, but where the customer is not known to reside or have traveled.
indicators.red_flag: Unexplained cash-deposit influx inconsistent with income / from ISIS-area ATMs
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D2 (Cash & instrument channel data (ATM/ABM, teller, money orders, prepaid)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a personal account whose inflow volume or wealth velocity is inconsistent with the customer's declared income, occupation, or stated source of funds, escalating when large credits lack a plausible origin for the customer's profile.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared income profile
build_logic.source: personal deposit ledger joined to onboarding income/occupation KYC data
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer suddenly adopts or increases their use of financial methods that conceal the ultimate source or end use of funds, for example P2P transfers, ATM withdrawals, third party processors, prepaid cards, virtual currency, or wire transfers.
indicators.red_flag: Sudden shift to source-obscuring channels (P2P / prepaid / VC / third-party processor)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer makes deposits in an account locally which are then withdrawn from other locations, including from abroad, where the individual is not known to reside or have traveled but where ISIS is prevalent.
indicators.red_flag: Local deposit → cross-border withdrawal in ISIS-prevalent geography (geographic mismatch)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer places virtual currency in a virtual currency wallet using an IP address in one location which is then withdrawn from virtual currency kiosks or converted to fiat currency by users with IP addresses in different locations where the individual is not known to reside or have traveled but where ISIS is prevalent.
indicators.red_flag: VC deposit/withdrawal IP-geography mismatch into ISIS-prevalent regions (VC kiosk cash-out)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators Related to the Financing of ISIS
indicators.flag: A customer’s account appears to have been accessed in multiple countries at the same time or within a very short time period, particularly if the account is accessed in countries where ISIS is prevalent.
indicators.red_flag: Impossible-travel concurrent multi-country account access (ISIS-prevalent geography)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D9 (Identity-verification, document & device/session telemetry), not currently held → source data first.
